source.citation: Thompson, D'Arcy W. (1917) On Growth and Form. Cambridge University Press. Ch. V 'The Forms of Cells', pp. 201-276; Figs. 61-67 (Plateau/Delaunay surfaces), 72-96 (protist and cell forms)

key_pages.p216-217: Laplace pressure p = T/R (one curvature) and p = T (1/R + 1/R') (two principal curvatures); the 'immensely important formula is due to Laplace (1806)'
key_pages.p218-219: Plateau's six surfaces of revolution of constant mean curvature: plane, sphere, cylinder, catenoid, unduloid, nodoid; Delaunay (1841) roulette construction (Fig. 61 A-C): rolling circle -> cylinder, rolling ellipse focus -> unduloid, degenerate ellipse -> string of spheres, parabola -> catenoid, hyperbola -> nodoid
key_pages.p222-223: Figs. 63-65: cylindrical, unduloid, nodoid and catenoid oil globules (Plateau's experiments)
key_pages.p223: 'In the unduloid ... the sum of the two [curvatures] must remain positive, as well as constant' -> the convex curvature at the neck exceeds the concave one
key_pages.p256: Fig. 84 'Various species of Lagena (after Brady)': 'This large and varied genus consists of flask-shaped shells, whose surface is simply that of an unduloid, or more frequently, like that of a flask itself, an unduloid combined with a portion of a sphere'
key_pages.p257: Lagena as a 'hanging drop drawn out to a long and slender neck'; Fig. 85 Darling's hanging drops 'are the most beautiful and perfect unduloids, with spherical ends'; Orbulina = 'a simple spherical drop'
key_pages.p261-262: longitudinal fluting of the body vs transverse pleating of the narrow neck (Fig. 86-87, Nodosaria scalaris) -- a wall-stiffness, not a surface-tension, effect
key_pages.p263: Fig. 89 Nodosaria, Rheophax, Sagrina: 'a constricted cylinder, or succession of unduloids'; chains built 'beginning with a simple unduloid Lagena, about whose neck ... another drop ... in turn assumed the unduloid, or lagenoid, form'

claim_statement: The forms of single cells and cell-like organisms (Plateau's oil globules; Lagena and other forams/protists) are surfaces of revolution from the minimal-surface catalogue: sphere, cylinder, unduloid, nodoid, catenoid.

claim_decomposition.C1_surface_of_revolution: The test is axisymmetric: a meridional (side-view) outline is bilaterally symmetric about the long axis.
claim_decomposition.C2_delaunay_membership: The meridional radius profile r(z) of a unilocular Lagena is a Delaunay (constant-mean-curvature) curve: an unduloid, or an unduloid joined C1 to a sphere (Thompson's own 'flask' qualification), with the drawn-out neck tending to the cylinder member.
claim_decomposition.C3_catalogue_closure: Only the Delaunay catalogue is needed (no free-form curve); the fit residual of the catalogue should be comparable to a free-form smooth curve with similar degrees of freedom and clearly better than a non-Delaunay null family.
claim_decomposition.C4_scope: Polythalamous (multi-chambered) tests are outside the claim; a single Delaunay surface should fit them worse (negative control).

E1_laplace_young.meaning: Pressure jump across a surface film of tension T with principal radii of curvature R_1, R_2; H = (kappa_1 + kappa_2)/2 is the mean curvature. Uniform pressure and tension imply H = const (constant mean curvature, CMC).

E2_cmc_surface_of_revolution.meaning: Mean curvature of the surface of revolution generated by rotating the meridian r = r(z) about the z-axis.
E2_cmc_surface_of_revolution.thompson_locus: p. 218 (stated verbally: 'surfaces of revolution ... six in all')

E3_delaunay_first_integral.formula: r / sqrt(1 + r'^2) - H * r^2 = C   (constant along the meridian)
E3_delaunay_first_integral.meaning: Integrating E2 once (multiply by r r' and integrate) gives the Delaunay first integral. At the neck and bulge r' = 0, so H r^2 - r + C = 0 has the two roots r_min, r_max with r_min + r_max = 1/H and r_min * r_max = C/H.

E4_kenmotsu_parametrisation.formula: r(s) = sqrt(1 + B^2 + 2 B sin(2 H s)) / (2 H);   z(s) = integral_0^s (1 + B sin(2 H t)) / sqrt(1 + B^2 + 2 B sin(2 H t)) dt
E4_kenmotsu_parametrisation.meaning: Arc-length parametrisation of every Delaunay surface with H != 0 (Kenmotsu 1980). B = 0 cylinder; 0 < B < 1 unduloid; B = 1 string of spheres of radius 1/H; B > 1 nodoid. Neck r_min = (1-B)/(2H), bulge r_max = (1+B)/(2H).
E4_kenmotsu_parametrisation.ellipse_roulette_link: Rolling-ellipse semi-axes a, b and focal half-distance c = sqrt(a^2 - b^2): a = (r_max + r_min)/2 = 1/(2H), c = (r_max - r_min)/2, so B = c/a is the eccentricity of Delaunay's rolling ellipse and r_min r_max = a^2 - c^2 = b^2.
E4_kenmotsu_parametrisation.catenoid: H = 0 member: r(z) = c cosh(z / c) (roulette of the parabola focus), minimal surface, not of the Kenmotsu family.

E5_neck_ratio.formula: rho = r_min / r_max = (1 - B) / (1 + B) = (a - c) / (a + c)
E5_neck_ratio.meaning: The single shape parameter of an unduloid up to scale; strictly decreasing in B on [0, 1]; rho = 1 cylinder, rho = 0 sphere string.

E6_unduloid_period.formula: Lambda = 4 a E(e), e = B = c/a, E = complete elliptic integral of the 2nd kind
E6_unduloid_period.meaning: Axial distance between successive necks (one 'bead'); Lambda = 2 pi a for the cylinder limit and 4a (= 2 sphere diameters) for the sphere limit.

E7_delaunay_flask_composite.formula: r(z) = sphere(R) for z in [0, R];  unduloid(H = (1+B)/(2R), B) from its bulge (r = R, s = pi/(4H)) to its neck (s = 3 pi/(4H));  cylinder r = R (1-B)/(1+B) of length L_neck
E7_delaunay_flask_composite.meaning: Thompson's 'unduloid combined with a portion of a sphere' made explicit: C1 join of the hemisphere equator to the unduloid bulge (both have r' = 0 and radius R), and C1 join of the unduloid neck to a cylindrical neck tube. Shape parameters: B (0..1), L_neck/R; scale R; placement z0.
E7_delaunay_flask_composite.note: Every piece is a member of the catalogue, so a good fit of this composite supports the claim exactly as Thompson qualified it.

E8_unduloid_bead.formula: r(z) from a single Kenmotsu unduloid (H, B) over an arc-length window [s_0, s_1] (at most one period), spindle-shaped Lagena with two pointed ends
E8_unduloid_bead.meaning: Pure-unduloid alternative member used for fusiform tests (Thompson: 'whose surface is simply that of an unduloid').

state_variables.z: axial coordinate along the symmetry axis (pixels in the image, normalised by r_max for comparison)
state_variables.r(z): meridional radius (half-width of the silhouette at height z)
state_variables.s: arc length along the meridian (Kenmotsu parameter)
state_variables.B: Kenmotsu/Delaunay shape parameter (= eccentricity of the rolling ellipse)
state_variables.R: sphere radius of the flask base

boundary_conditions.unduloid: r'(s) = 0 at necks (s = 3 pi/(4H) mod pi/H) and bulges (s = pi/(4H) mod pi/H); profile periodic in s with period pi/H
boundary_conditions.flask_base: r(0) = 0 at the aboral pole of the sphere; r' -> infinity (vertical tangent) at the pole
boundary_conditions.flask_neck: truncated at the aperture, r = r_neck, free end
boundary_conditions.fit_domain: only the lateral silhouette between the aboral pole and the apertural lip is fitted; ornament (costae, reticulation) is averaged out by the half-width profile

empirical_biological_claims.text: Orbulina is a perfect sphere (pelagic, symmetric to all external forces).
Lagena is flask-shaped: an unduloid, or an unduloid combined with a portion of a sphere.
Lagena forms like a hanging drop drawn out into a slender neck (Darling's ethyl-benzoate drops are 'perfect unduloids with spherical ends').
Flattened Lagena variants arise where axial symmetry of position was lost.
Nodosaria/Rheophax/Sagrina are chains of unduloids built lagena-by-lagena.
Body fluting is longitudinal, neck pleating transverse (wall stiffness).
